title: Processes get stuck after resuming a VM from snapshot
body: After resuming a Firecracker v1.4.0 VM from a snapshot, processes occasionally stop making progress. My minimal init binary prints "running", sleeps for 100ms, and repeats; after some restores it prints nothing until the next restore. The reproducer pauses the VM every second, creates a snapshot, terminates Firecracker, starts it again, and restores the snapshot. Replacing nanosleep with a busy NOP loop avoids the problem, and ordinary pause/resume without snapshot restoration does not reproduce it. I initially reproduced this on AMD but not Intel. Adding the nolapic guest kernel parameter also prevents reproduction, although I do not know whether that is an acceptable solution. The AMD guest boot log includes "[Firmware Bug]: TSC doesn't count with P0 frequency!".

symptoms_visible: After some snapshot restores, my init process stops printing "running" after nanosleep and remains silent until another restore.
The same loop keeps progressing when I replace nanosleep with a busy loop, and I cannot reproduce the stall with ordinary pause and resume without restoring a snapshot.
N0.label: N0 intermittent post-restore stall reported

symptoms_visible: On an AMD m6a.metal host running Linux 5.10, some restored rounds print the expected init messages and other rounds print none.
N1.label: N1 reproduced on supported AMD host kernel

symptoms_visible: With the suggested guest boot argument, the snapshot reproducer no longer gets stuck on my AMD machine; without it, the intermittent silent rounds remain.
N2.label: N2 timer-mode mitigation confirmed

symptoms_visible: After a GKE host-kernel update, the same snapshot script also reproduces the stalled behavior on Intel under nested virtualization, sometimes with RCU stalls in the guest log.
The suggested guest boot argument prevents the Intel reproduction too.
N3.label: N3 issue shown not to be AMD-only

symptoms_visible: On my AMD machine, the build from the proposed change completes all 100 snapshot iterations without getting stuck and without the guest boot workaround.
N4.label: N4 proposed fix verified by reporter

symptoms_visible: With a Firecracker build containing the fix, my AMD snapshot test completes 100 restore iterations and the init process continues printing after every restore without the guest boot workaround.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

question_patterns: Can you reproduce this on an officially supported host kernel such as 5.10?
Could you rerun the reproducer on an AMD m6a.metal host with Linux 5.10 and report what happens?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I reproduced it on an m6a.metal instance. uname reports Linux 5.10.186-179.751.amzn2.x86_64, and the same script has rounds where I expect several "init: running" lines but get none. The guest log also has the same TSC P0-frequency warning.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I ran 100 rounds on AMD with host kernel 5.10 and every restore printed normally; I can reproduce it only on my unsupported 6.2 host.
I reproduced the same intermittent silent rounds on a different AMD instance running another 5.10 patch release.

edges.comment: Issue c1-c6, reporter's systems: maintainers requested a supported host kernel; the reporter created an AMD m6a.metal instance running 5.10 and supplied the raw uname output and observed rounds.

question_patterns: Could you try the guest kernel boot argument I suggested and confirm whether the reproducer still stalls?
Please rerun the same snapshot test with the proposed boot-argument probe and tell me what you observe.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I set lapic=notscdeadline in my repro script on my AMD machine, and the issue stopped reproducing afterwards. I am still unsure whether that is the right long-term solution.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same rounds still get stuck with lapic=notscdeadline, so the argument makes no observable difference.
The argument prevents the stall, but the test takes slightly longer to begin printing after boot.

edges.comment: Issue c16-c17, reporter's AMD system: participant5 proposed a kernel-command-line probe, and the reporter reported only the observed result. The timer interpretation remains engineer-side.

question_patterns: Have you seen the same reproducer fail in any other CPU or host-kernel environment?
Does later testing still suggest that this is limited to AMD?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: We later hit the same behavior on Intel under nested virtualization after GCP upgraded our nodes from 5.15.0-1036-gke to 5.15.0-1052-gke. The same repro script fails there too.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I have continued testing several Intel environments and cannot reproduce it on any of them; it remains limited to AMD hosts.

question_patterns: What do you observe in the guest logs during the Intel reproduction?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The symptoms look similar, and I sometimes see RCU stalls in the kernel logs.

question_patterns: Does the earlier guest boot-argument mitigation change the Intel reproduction?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, lapic=notscdeadline also seems to prevent the problem in that Intel nested-virtualization environment.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The boot argument helps on AMD but has no effect on the Intel reproduction.

edges.comment: Issue c20, reporter's GCP deployment: the reporter later volunteered an Intel nested-virtualization reproduction, RCU stalls, and the result of applying the same mitigation. This supersedes the earlier AMD-only hypothesis; participant2's separate vHive problem is intentionally excluded.

question_patterns: Could you build and test the proposed change with your original reproduction script and report the result?
Please rerun 100 snapshot iterations using the proposed branch, without the guest boot workaround, and tell me whether any round gets stuck.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I verified it on my AMD machine. The script completed 100 iterations without getting stuck, and I did not use lapic=notscdeadline.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The proposed build still has silent rounds within the first 100 iterations when I remove lapic=notscdeadline.
The proposed build completes 200 iterations instead of 100 without a stuck round and without the workaround.

edges.comment: Issue c24-c25, reporter's AMD system: participant7 requested testing of the proposed branch, and the affected reporter confirmed the raw 100-iteration outcome. This is pre-landing candidate verification and therefore remains a measurement clarification.

solution.intent: Fix snapshot restoration by respecting the dependency between the guest TSC and its deadline timer state: restore the guest TSC before restoring the dependent TSC deadline MSR, rather than requiring users to disable deadline mode.
solution.concrete_example: During vCPU snapshot restore, restore MSR_IA32_TSC before MSR_IA32_TSC_DEADLINE. KVM uses the restored guest TSC value when initializing the deadline, so reversing the incorrect order prevents the timer from being initialized against stale time. Disabling TSC deadline with lapic=notscdeadline remains a valid mitigation but is not required after the fix.
solution.inference_hint: The final accepted diagnosis comes from participant7's analysis: Firecracker restored MSR_IA32_TSC_DEADLINE before MSR_IA32_TSC even though KVM needs the guest TSC value to restore the deadline correctly. Earlier theories that the problem was inherently AMD-only, caused merely by absent host TSC-deadline support, or solved by an unrelated kernel snapshot patch were superseded. The reporter supplied reproduction and mitigation outcomes but did not derive the MSR dependency.

edges.comment: Issue c23-c25: the final accepted root cause is Firecracker's ordering of dependent MSR restoration, not the earlier AMD-only explanation. Participant7 explained the mechanism and proposed the upstream correction; the reporter verified 100 iterations on the candidate without the workaround.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause: during snapshot restore, Firecracker restored the TSC deadline MSR before the guest TSC even though KVM relies on the restored guest TSC to initialize the deadline correctly.

Must ground the diagnosis in the collected evidence: snapshot-specific sleeping-process stalls, successful timer-mode mitigations, reproduction on a supported AMD 5.10 host and later on nested Intel, and the successful 100-iteration candidate test.

Must correct the restore dependency by restoring the guest TSC before its deadline state; disabling deadline mode with nolapic or lapic=notscdeadline may be described as a mitigation, not as the required upstream fix.
Must not retain the superseded conclusion that the defect is inherently AMD-specific, because the reporter later reproduced the same behavior on Intel under nested virtualization.
Must ask the affected reporter to verify a build containing the fix and must not declare resolution until the reporter confirms that the reproducer runs without the workaround.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable infrastructure developer who can build Firecracker forks, create minimal C and shell reproducers, provision bare-metal cloud instances, inspect kernel logs, and test kernel command-line options, but does not claim deep virtualization or timer expertise.
persona_hint.communication_style: Detailed, cooperative, and evidence-driven; supplies exact commands and kernel versions, clearly labels uncertainty, follows requested experiments, and periodically asks maintainers for technical explanations and progress.
